flashcard_questions.q: Which 1896 Supreme Court ruling established the doctrine of 'separate but equal'?
How many people were lynched in the United States between 1882 and 1968?
What age was Emmett Till when he was murdered in Mississippi in 1955?
Which all-Black fighter pilot squadron excelled in combat during the Second World War?
Which newspaper launched the 'Double V' campaign in 1942?
Which executive order did Truman sign in 1948 to desegregate the US armed forces?
Who was the NAACP's chief lawyer, leading its legal challenges to segregation?
On what date did the Supreme Court rule in Brown v. Board of Education?
Which Chief Justice declared that 'separate educational facilities are inherently unequal'?
Which governor used the Arkansas National Guard to block the Little Rock Nine?
Who became the first Black student to enrol at the University of Mississippi in 1962?
How many days did the Montgomery Bus Boycott last?
On what date was Rosa Parks arrested in Montgomery?
Which teenager refused to give up her bus seat nine months before Rosa Parks?
Which organisation did Martin Luther King Jr. help found in 1957 to coordinate Southern campaigns?

notes: 15 cards: 5 person to significance, 4 ruling-or-law to name, 3 statistic, 2 event to date, 1 organisation. Dropped Browder v. Gayle so it does not interfere with Brown and Plessy; dropped the 67-minute acquittal to stay inside 15.
